content: 1. The metabolism of clomipramine may be affected by hepatic enzyme CYP1A2, leading to an increase in its levels or effects. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 2. Cyclophosphamide can increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by influencing the metabolism mediated by hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 3. Danazol may elevate the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering its metabolism through hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 4. Ethinylestradiol may reduce the oxidative metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), potentially increasing their serum concentrations. This could lead to an elevated risk of adverse effects associated with TCAs. 5. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of duloxetine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 6. Enasidenib may either increase or decrease the concentrations of combined hormonal contraceptives. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 7. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of eplerenone by influencing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 8. Felbamate decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 9. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of frovatriptan by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 10. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of ramelteon by influencing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 11. Rosuvastatin increases the levels of ethinylestradiol through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 12. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of ruxolitinib (both systemic and topical forms) by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 13. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of tizanidine through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 14. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of caffeine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 15. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of bendamustine by decreasing its metabolism. Bendamustine is metabolized by CYP1A2, and ethinylestradiol, as a weak CYP1A2 inhibitor, may elevate bendamustine plasma concentrations. 16. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of atogepant by influencing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 17. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of axitinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 18. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of asenapine by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 19. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of alosetron by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 20. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of alprazolam by decreasing its metabolism. Ethinylestradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, leading to increased serum concentrations of co-administered benzodiazepines. 21. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of amitriptyline by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Estrogens and progestins may decrease the effects of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) while increasing TCA plasma concentrations and adverse effects. 22. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of amoxapine by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Estrogens and progestins may decrease the effects of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) while increasing TCA plasma concentrations and adverse effects. 23. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of amoxicillin by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of ampicillin by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of anastrozole by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 26. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of antipyrene by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 27. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of atorvastatin by influencing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 28. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of atazanavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir may also increase or decrease levels of norgestimate. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 29. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of bosentan by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 30. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of brigatinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Brigatinib induces CYP3A4 in vitro, and co-administration with hormonal contraceptives may result in decreased concentrations and loss of efficacy. Women should use effective non-hormonal contraception during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last brigatinib dose. 31. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of butabarbital by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 32. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of calaspargase pegol through an unknown mechanism. Due to the potential for an indirect interaction with oral contraceptives, concomitant use is not recommended. Non-oral contraceptive methods are advised for females of childbearing potential. 33. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of carbamazepine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Carbamazepine may also decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by the same mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 34. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of cefaclor by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of cefadroxil by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 36. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of cefazolin by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 37. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of cefdinir by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 38. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of cefepime by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of cefepime/enmetazobactam by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 40. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of cefixime by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised.
